subject.title: Feature request: turn-based / rolling session pruning (not only cache-ttl)

question: Which public active-session pruning contract should OpenClaw support for this issue: an opt-in rolling/turn trigger, a cache-ttl nested option, a usage-pressure TTL bypass, or no built-in trigger yet?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines public context-pruning config and the default cost-versus-context-retention behavior automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve opt-in rolling trigger
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default rolling or turn-age pruning trigger that runs before each model call while preserving existing cache-ttl behavior for current users.

options.title: Use usage-pressure TTL bypass
options.body: Prefer a force-prune threshold that only bypasses TTL under high estimated context pressure, reducing behavior change at the cost of not being strictly turn-based.

options.title: Defer to broader context design
options.body: Keep the current cache-ttl contract and handle active-session pruning through a future context-engine or pruning-hook design instead.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in rolling trigger
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default rolling or turn-age pruning trigger that runs before each model call while preserving existing cache-ttl behavior for current users.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the cache-ttl public config surface and is the strongest available owner for the product/config contract choice.
